attacks.claim: The embargo badge sets text to #ffffff over var(--surface), which is #ffffff in the default light theme. The label is effectively invisible (about 1:1 contrast), failing WCAG 1.4.3 on a stated release requirement.

The unpublish control is a span with only an onClick handler and an aria-hidden icon. It has no role, tabIndex, key handler, accessible name, or focus-visible style, so keyboard-only and screen-reader editors cannot reach or identify the destructive action (WCAG 2.1.1, 4.1.2).

The unpublish control renders for every viewer of published rows. The diff shows no role or permission check, and server-side authorization for onUnpublish is not evidenced, so the client alone does not establish who may pull a live story.
attacks.evidence: {draft.status === "published" && (...unpublish span...)} ABSENT: role/permission gate or server-side authz for onUnpublish

attacks.claim: onUnpublish is awaited with no try/catch, pending state, or error feedback. A failed request produces an unhandled rejection and the row gives no indication of failure; rapid clicks may open multiple confirm dialogs.
attacks.evidence: if (ok) await onUnpublish(draft.id); ABSENT: catch, busy state, or user-visible failure

attacks.claim: The confirm copy says the story is removed from the site and returned to drafts, but says nothing about syndicated, wire, or cached copies that may already be public. The public effect of an early-released story is not shown to be reversible, and no republish or downstream handling is evidenced.
attacks.evidence: "will be removed from the site and returned to drafts." ABSENT: syndication notification, cache purge, republish path

attacks.claim: The PR asserts WCAG AA conformance but provides no contrast measurements, screenshots in either theme, keyboard or screen-reader verification, or tests. The tokens.css hunk is also truncated inside the dark block, so the full dark token set cannot be checked.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: contrast ratios, screenshots, keyboard/SR verification, tests; tokens.css hunk ends at "--text: #e7e9ee;"

attacks.claim: Embargo state is computed from the browser clock at render time and never refreshed, so a long-open queue can show a stale badge and a skewed client clock can show the wrong state.
attacks.evidence: const embargoed = draft.embargoUntil !== null && new Date(draft.embargoUntil) > new Date();

attacks.claim: The lift time has no timezone label even though the PR says it is shown in newsroom time, so editors in other zones cannot tell which zone is displayed.
attacks.evidence: format string "MMM d, HH:mm" with no zone suffix

attacks.claim: The unpublish control is an unlabeled trash icon with a small 6px target and only a hover state. Trash suggests deletion rather than return-to-drafts, which invites mis-clicks.
Showing embargo lift times to every queue role and unpublishing embargo-relevant content with no audit record are not confirmed against newsroom policy.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: role clearance for embargo visibility; ABSENT: audit logging in handleUnpublish

attacks.claim: The PR says 'one-click' while the flow includes a confirm dialog, overstating the improvement; the embargo rule is also duplicated client-side with no shared source of truth.
attacks.evidence: "a one-click unpublish action on each queue row. Unpublish still goes through the standard confirm dialog."

attacks.claim: e.stopPropagation() is unnecessary because the unpublish control is a sibling of the open button, and the draft.embargoUntil! assertion relies on the embargoed guard, which is fragile under refactoring.
attacks.evidence: async function handleUnpublish(e: React.MouseEvent) { e.stopPropagation(); ... } draft.embargoUntil!
